47ad4ae86d: Chord diagrams: looking at the fretboard with the guitar stood upright
929d077b4a: Vertical lines are strings: the far left is the thickest, string 6, and the far right the thinnest, string 1 (turned 90 degrees from tab)
f4e6372a4b: Horizontal lines are frets: the thick line at the top is the nut, then frets 1, 2 and 3 going down
4644b7e523: Dots show where to press, and the number inside is the finger: 1 index, 2 middle, 3 ring, 4 little
51040d004a: ○ means play the open string, × means skip it: when you strum, start from the first string that should be played
53ef4fe928: C: start with the ring finger and place fingers from low to high
d5195d6743: Pluck string by string; every one should ring
7a1d28e117: Order to place fingers: ring finger string 5 fret 3 → middle string 4 fret 2 → index string 2 fret 1
40c28af2c0: Common problem: if the pad of the middle finger touches string 3, or the index touches string 1, the note goes dead
e5afaa48fd: Am: only one finger different from C
7afff8e2b6: Only the ring finger moves, from string 5 fret 3 to string 3 fret 2
e25ff958c3: Strum Am from open string 5, skipping string 6
120ef95897: Listen closely: Am is a minor chord, darker than C with a touch of sadness
d1603d4c18: G: spread your fingers and let all six strings ring
14c76633fc: Pluck string by string; string 6 should ring too
66cb35ca68: Middle finger string 6 fret 3, index string 5 fret 2, ring finger string 1 fret 3
cd8cb12f21: Drop your wrist and keep your palm off the neck so your fingers can spread
f7d0cfd06c: Small F: the index finger lies flat across two strings
2b9fc71e32: Lay the index finger flat across strings 1 and 2 at fret 1, using the side nearer the thumb, where the bone is firmer and presses down more easily
634f7333e3: Middle finger string 3 fret 2, ring finger string 4 fret 3; skip strings 6 and 5
b08b2a998f: The full barre F (all six strings) waits until Chapter 8

9b0d920567: String 2 fret 1, strings 3 and 4 fret 2, string 6 crossed out: the answer is Am. Only the ring finger differs from C.
9fed82d078: Close your eyes and tell which chord you're hearing

3a8ac78ce3: The harder you press, the louder the chord
58301bbadf: MythPosition matters more than strength: close to the fret, fingertips upright, and a light press makes it ring.
65bb23c711: Muted notes mostly come from a finger touching the next string
9ce68c39ee: FactIf your finger isn't upright enough, its pad presses on the next string. Pluck string by string once and you'll find where.
dfa84bbaa3: MythKeep your left-hand nails short so your fingertips can stand up.
72975dfc9c: Look at your hand first, then strum
16fa77a056: MythYou can look at first, but the goal is to place your fingers with your eyes closed, leaving your eyes free to read the chart.
d331820d67: F is too hard, so it's fine to skip it for now
7eb0e1e99b: MythSmall F is your way into barre chords; get it now and Chapter 8 will be much easier.
f97e562914: If you can't change in time, strum the open strings
1f2e000b6b: FactKeep the beat going and listeners will hardly notice. Your fingers will get faster with each change.
